Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

instead adverb and preposition

in place of

also instead of, in place of, in someone’s place, in someone’s stead

classical

Plaut. Most. 1131b: ego ībō prō tē, sī tibi nōn libet
Ter. And. 200: ego prō tē molam
Traupman 333: instead of, prō (+ abl)

prō (+ ablative)

preposition with the ablative

instead of, in place of, for

One person or thing put in the place of another (Lewis & Short: “with the notion of replacement or substitution”).

Other words

  • nōn … sed — not … but (this instead of that)

    conjunctions, joining any two parts of a sentence · also used · classical · Gell. 7.13.2: nōn cuppēdiās cibōrum, sed argūtiās quaestiōnum; Hor. S. 2.2.120–121: nōn piscibus urbe petītīs, sed pullō atque haedō

    Where English says “instead of doing”, Latin sets the two side by side: not this, but that. To prefer one action to another, potius quam (see rather).

  • locō (+ genitive) — in place of, as

    ablative of locus, with a genitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.3.6: crīminis locō putent esse quod vīvam

    Something counted as, or standing in for, something else.

Examples

  • Quīn venīs? — Prōmitte: ego ībō prō tē, sī tibi nōn libet.

    Why won’t you come? — Say yes: I’ll go instead of you, if you don’t feel like it.Plaut. Most. 1131–1131b

  • conjectābāmus ad cēnulam nōn cuppēdiās cibōrum, sed argūtiās quaestiōnum

    to our little dinner we each brought, instead of delicacies, clever questionsGell. 7.13.2

See also rather.

SourcesLewis & Short: pro · Lewis & Short: sed · Lewis & Short: locus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 333.
